transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

Yes — on many Beko washer-dryers this can be normal.

Unlike a separate tumble dryer, many washer-dryers use cold mains water during the drying cycle to cool a condenser. The warm, damp air from the drum is cooled so the moisture turns back into water, which is then pumped away. That can sound like:

• water entering the machine intermittently or for long periods
• the drain pump running / water going down the drain
• repeated filling and draining while it is drying

So it can use a surprising amount of water even if the clothes were already fairly dry.

A few things to check:

• Is it actually getting hot and drying? If yes, the water use is probably part of normal operation.
• Is the water tap fully on? It needs a water supply to dry properly on these models.
• Is it continuously filling even when switched off or not in use? That would not be normal and could indicate an inlet-valve fault.
• Does it fail to dry, show an error code, leak, or run for far longer than expected? Then it may need investigation.
• Ensure the drain hose isn’t pushed too far down the standpipe or fitted in a way that could cause siphoning.

If you send the exact Beko model number from the door frame or rating label, I can tell you whether that particular model uses water-cooled condensation and what its normal drying behaviour should be.

Thank you. The model number on the label is WDL742431W. To answer your questions: yes, it dries the clothes well, there's no error code, no leaks, and no water comes through when the machine is off. Is the water use during drying definitely normal for this model?

Yes — for the Beko WDL742431W, water entering and being pumped away during drying is normal.

It is a condenser washer-dryer, rather than a vented dryer. During drying it uses cold mains water to cool the condenser system: moisture removed from the clothes condenses into water and is then pumped out through the drain. This can mean you hear both the inlet water and drain pump during much of the drying programme.

Given that yours:

• dries properly,
• has no error messages,
• does not leak, and
• does not admit water when switched off,

there is no obvious sign of a fault. Keep the water tap on whenever using a drying programme — it needs the water supply to dry correctly.

It is less water-efficient than a separate heat-pump tumble dryer, so the amount of water used can seem counter-intuitive, but it is expected behaviour for this type of washer-dryer.
